item.text: The project was absent, so I initialized it from the supplied snapshot. The assurance view preserves both DUT identity claims and flags their disagreement as blocking. The JW-specific analysis remains conditional: TXU0304 fits the declared SPI directions, but the physical DUT identity, pinout, electrical budget, and supply design remain unresolved.

actions.summary: Capture physical marking/package and traceable procurement order; reconcile JW/JV with matching manufacturer documentation while retaining both original claims.
Obtain exact programmer documentation, supported clocks and timing; plan later authorized voltage-under-load validation.
Select available TXU0304 orderable package and footprint if still appropriate; map logical channels to verified package pins and resolve all DUT control pins.
Obtain complete VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL, load and delay data; close both directions' timing budget and select supported SPI rate.
Design applicable DUT rail, current budget, decoupling, protection, sequencing and fail-safe OE. 1.8 V remains only the declared target.

Prepare schematic and PCB; complete ERC/DRC and independent review. Define separately authorized bench checks for rails, signal levels, timing and startup; no measurements or authorization currently exist.

architecture_candidates.summary: Rejected for declared JW 1.8 V branch because 3.3 V exceeds VCC+0.4 V. No conclusion about undocumented JV limits.

Conditional family candidate for the declared JW standard SPI branch; A at declared host 3.3 V, B at proposed DUT 1.8 V are within documented translator supply ranges. Physical application held pending identity and electrical validation.

One device with common host-side/DUT-side orientation cannot provide three forward plus one reverse simultaneous channels: each two-channel group shares direction. Rail range includes 3.3 V and 1.8 V but does not solve direction grouping. Other multi-device arrangements are unassessed.
